html:
A small battle in 559 near the village of Melantias, about 30 km from Constantinople, the last fight of the general Belisarius.

In March 559 the Kutrigur Huns under their leader Zabergan crossed the frozen Danube and raided Thrace and Greece. One force came close to the capital, where the walls had been damaged by the earthquake of 557. Justinian called the old general out of retirement. Belisarius had only a few hundred veterans, eked out with civilians and farmers. He set an ambush in a narrow place, used noise and dust to make his force look bigger, and attacked the Kutrigur cavalry from several sides. They fled, and the threat to the city ended.

Justinian then paid the Kutrigurs to go home and turned their rivals, the Utigurs, against them. The battle is described by the historian Agathias.
sum: A small battle in 559 near the village of Melantias, about 30 km from Constantinople, the last fight of the general Belisarius.
